title: KV stripe-horizon orchestrator and adaptive anti-fragmentation plan
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's KV cache on GPU has degradation modes driven by allocation fragmentation interacting with continuous batching. Small, scattered allocations (short-lived prompts, many tokens) create micro-gaps that reduce usable contiguous memory for large KV entries and cause more frequent relocations, which in turn increases tail latency and GPU memory bandwidth usage.

Goal:
Design and implement a new allocation orchestration layer ("stripe-horizon orchestrator") that: (1) reduces fragmentation by aligning allocations to time-aware stripes, (2) cooperates with the continuous batching planner to produce contiguous placement for long-lived KV entries, and (3) provides a low-overhead background compaction/relocation mechanism with predictable CPU/GPU cost. Target impact: reduce fragmentation ratio by >=30% on mixed workloads and keep P95 token latency regression <=2%.

High-level design:
- Stripe Horizon: divide GPU KV memory into logical "stripes" sized to typical long-lived KV footprints per model class. Each stripe is a placement unit; allocs prefer empty stripes to avoid micro-gaps.
- Horizon Window: allocator exposes a short time horizon (e.g., 50-200ms) to the batching layer. The batching planner marks requests expected to produce long-term KV (e.g., first tokens from a chat turn) so those allocations are steered into contiguous stripe regions.
- Warm Reserve Buckets: maintain small reserved contiguous buckets per stripe that are only used for allocations predicted to be long-lived. Short-lived allocations use a separate slab-like pool that is aggressively reclaimed.
- Topology-aware placement: consider GPU NUMA-like topology and per-GPU allocation hotness to avoid cross-chip scattering when serving multi-GPU shards.
- Background micro-relocation daemon: time-windowed compaction that runs when batch fill < threshold or GPU utilization is below a configurable level. This daemon relocates low-temperature tokens into freed stripes with a bounded relocation budget (bytes/sec).
- Eviction & Hinting hooks: continuous batching runtime will emit eviction hints (soft-promote / soft-demote) for token caches to guide relocation priority and avoid moving hot KV.

Detailed algorithm parameters (initial):
- stripe_size: 2-8MB (tunable per-model family)
- horizon_ms: 100ms default, exposes a hint to the batching planner
- warm_reserve_per_stripe: 4 slots (adjust to model footprint)
- compaction_threshold: fragmentation_ratio > 0.20 triggers background compaction windows
- relocation_budget: 128MB/s per GPU (controlled by feature flag)
- prewarm_window: when a route sees >50% repeated tokens in 10s, mark for contiguous placement

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive compaction minimizes fragmentation but consumes GPU memory BW and can add jitter to latency; we favor a bounded budget and idle-triggered windows to limit cost.
- Larger stripe sizes reduce fragmentation but can increase internal waste for many tiny entries; warm-reserve + slab pools mitigate this.
- Tighter coupling with the batching planner yields better placement but increases cross-team surface (runtime <-> allocator API). We will iterate by exposing a small stable hint API rather than tight integration initially.

Observability & telemetry (required):
- fragmentation_ratio: total_free_fragments_bytes / total_memory_bytes (target <0.15)
- avg_contiguous_run_size: distribution of largest contiguous free ranges
- relocation_bytes/sec and relocation_ops/sec
- avg_alloc_latency and p95_alloc_latency (ms)
- KV_hit_rate and KV_eviction_rate per-model
- batch_fill_ratio and batch_size_distribution
- SLO regressions: p50/p95 token latency comparisons vs baseline

Acceptance criteria (before rollout):
- Unit and integration tests covering stripe allocation, warm-reserve behavior, relocation daemon, and eviction hint handling.
- Load test on representative workloads (chat-like, long-context generation, mixed microprompts) showing >=30% reduction in fragmentation_ratio and <=2% P95 latency regression on 3 GPU types (A100, H100, T4-equivalent).
- Telemetry dashboards and alerts: fragmentation_ratio > 0.20 alert, relocation_budget_exceeded alert.
- Feature gate and rollback path implemented (allocator config flag per cluster/route).

Implementation plan & milestones:
1) Design doc & API (this ticket) — include simple hint API for batching planner — owner: Miguel — due 2025-02-18.
2) PoC in allocator: stripe bookkeeping and warm-reserve pools, simulated allocator tests — due 2025-02-28.
3) Integrate minimal hinting from batching planner (no invasive runtime changes) — due 2025-03-07.
4) Micro-relocation daemon and compaction windows with relocation budget enforcement — due 2025-03-14.
5) Canary rollout on internal dedicated cluster + load tests — due 2025-03-21.
6) Full rollout gated by metrics and RTC sign-off — due 2025-04-01.

Rollout and rollout flags:
- feature_flag: kv_stripe_horizon_v1 (off by default)
- config knobs: stripe_size, horizon_ms, compaction_threshold, relocation_budget, warm_reserve_count
- canary: 5% of requests on dedicated clusters, then 20%, then 100% if metrics good

Testing matrix:
- Synthetic fragmentation workloads (many small allocations interleaved with occasional big entries)
- Production replay of 72h traffic slice on dedicated hardware
- Multi-model co-tenancy tests (to measure cross-tenant interference)
- Stress tests with relocation budget disabled to observe worst-case behaviour

Dependencies:
- ENG-314159 (ghost-slab-kv-gpu-compaction) — reuse compaction plumbing
- ENG-612358 (token-residency-shard-controller) — for some placement signals
- runtime scheduling team for ensuring relocation daemon QoS on GPU side

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: relocation increases latency jitter. Mitigation: strict relocation_budget, perform relocations during idle windows and use cooperative evacuation (drain before move).
- Risk: mispredicted warm-reserve usage wastes memory. Mitigation: telemetry and automatic decay of reserve usage; fall back to slab pool if reserve underutilized.
- Risk: cross-team API churn with batching planner. Mitigation: keep hint surface minimal (three hints: LONG_LIVED, SHORT_LIVED, NO_PREFERENCE).
